questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of ControlValueAccessor?

options.text: To bridge Angular's forms API and a custom component's UI so it behaves like a native control

questions.explanation: CVA lets any component work with formControlName/[formControl]/ngModel by syncing value, touched, and disabled state.

questions.prompt: Which CVA method handles the model → view direction (e.g. setValue, patchValue, reset)?
questions.explanation: writeValue updates the component's internal state when the FormControl's value changes programmatically.

questions.prompt: Why does the NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR provider need forwardRef(() => MyComponent)?

options.text: Because the provider is evaluated in the class's own decorator metadata, before the class identifier is fully initialized
It is optional and never needed

questions.explanation: forwardRef defers resolving the self-reference until Angular actually needs it.

questions.prompt: What happens if you forget multi: true on the NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR provider?

options.text: Your provider replaces the list of accessors instead of joining it, which can break others or cause 'no value accessor' errors
The component throws a compile error

questions.explanation: NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR is a multi-provider token; multi: true adds to the list rather than replacing it.

options.text: No — it only syncs value, touched, and disabled; validation uses Validators or the Validator/NG_VALIDATORS interface

questions.explanation: Value synchronization and validation are intentionally separate concerns with separate tokens.

questions.prompt: Match each ControlValueAccessor method to its role.

pairs.right: Model → view: update UI from the FormControl
Store the callback to call on user value changes
Store the callback to call on blur/touch

questions.explanation: Together these four methods implement the full contract Angular's forms directives expect.
